{"id":"owc-guest-turn-latency","title":"A guest macrotask turn costs 1.25 ms, 40x the host's, and the hub defers every delivery by one","subject":"Two scheduling sites, neither of them in the transport code, set the floor on every streaming workload in the container. Measured at HEAD 02e1ab2 with 16 MiB over loopback, two guest processes, 64 KiB writes (machine never idle, load 15-29): the hub delivers in fixed 64 KiB pieces -- 256 'data' events whether the guest writes 16 KiB, 64 KiB or 256 KiB at a time -- and each one costs 2.0 ms, so 16 MiB takes 516 ms against host Node 24.15's 31 ms for the identical script. (1) runtime/guest/loader.ts:847 scheduleTimer() clamps any delay below 1 ms up to 1 ms ('if (!(delay >= 1)) delay = 1'), and setImmediateImpl calls it with 0, so guest setImmediate costs the same 1.25 ms/turn as setTimeout(f,0) and setTimeout(f,1); host Node prices those three at 0.030, 1.250 and 1.170 ms, so setImmediate -- the one the runtime's own streams use -- is 40x out. (2) network/virtual/hub.ts:438 schedule() wraps every delivery in setTimeout(..., 0), which cannot be finer than libuv's 1 ms floor; hub.ts:454 offer() does the same. Routing every host-side 0 ms timer onto the check phase, without touching a repo file (a global setTimeout shim in the driver), moves TCP upload 516 -> 453 ms and HTTP/2 upload 2045 -> 1207 ms but leaves the per-turn cost at 1.285 ms, which is what pins it: the clamp is in the guest, not on the host. Neither site is in this shard's grant (loader.ts and hub.ts); process.ts's own capabilityContext.deliver/deliverBytes setTimeout(..., 0) was changed to setImmediate and measured as inert (300 fs.promises round trips: 0.937 vs 0.970 ms/op), so it was reverted.","session_id":"adv7-exec-guest-perf","status":"pending","classification":"REPO","acceptance_criteria":["guest setImmediate measures within about 2x of host Node 24.15's setImmediate (0.030 ms/turn), while setTimeout(f, 0) keeps the host's 1 ms behaviour","16 MiB over loopback between two guest processes measures within about 2x of host Node on TCP and HTTP/1.1","the virtual hub schedules a delivery on the check phase, not on a 0 ms timer"],"witness_plan":"In packages/core: run a guest program that chains 200 setImmediate hops and prints ms/turn, beside the same on host Node 24.15; then run the 16 MiB loopback bench (TCP, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, upload and download) and compare each cell with the host column.","owner":"adv7-exec-guest-perf"}

{"paths":["Readme.md","packages/core/src/process/executors/node/runtime/capabilities/child.ts","packages/core/src/process/executors/shell/process.ts"],"message":"child: a piped stdin reaches the line, and a timeout ends the sleep it bounds

A `sh -c <line>` child thrown away what its parent wrote on the stdin pipe it was given:
`spawn('sh', ['-c', 'cat'])` closed with no input at all where a host's waits, and every
shape that writes and then ends -- two chunks, a delayed write, `stdin.end(str)`, a write
made on 'spawn' -- printed nothing. The shell's own line never read the pipe: `execute`
ran the line as soon as the process started and the parent's write could not arrive before

waits for the parent's end of file before it runs, which is what a host's `sh -c 'cat'`

operand were already right; only the order differed.

The host's order is the one `ls -f` prints, and `dirOrder` already reproduces it
for `-f` in this same module, so `walkRoot` takes the order it walks in as an
optional argument and chmod passes `dirOrder`. Every other walk still sorts, so
`find` and `-delete` keep the order a reproducible listing needs.

Measured against /bin/sh (bash 3.2) on this machine, 2026-10-23, both sides run
in a tree the wheel group owns, which is the group the container's own /app has
and the one that makes the host refuse the setgid bit as the container does:

{"message":"shell: name a directory wherever `cat` meets one

`cat` named a directory only where `lstat` said so, so a link to one was
read as a file and printed the `{}` a read of a directory leaves, with
status 0: `ln -s d l; cat l` is now `cat: l: Is a directory` and 1, the
link resolved through the table `ln` wrote, and `ln -s nope l; cat l` is
`No such file or directory` instead of a silent success. A directory put
on the standard input is named the way the host's `cat` names it -- `cat
< d` is `cat: stdin: Is a directory` -- which is the utility's own
complaint and not the shell's, so the redirection leaves what it opened
for the command that reads it to name.

A script's executability was decided by its shebang alone, so a 644 or
000 file behind `#!/bin/sh` ran and a 755 file with no shebang was
`Permission denied` and 126. The mode `chmod` recorded now decides: with
no execute bit a script is `sh: ./s: Permission denied` and 126, and with
one a file no shebang names runs as a script of its own, the way a host
answers ENOEXEC. A file copied into the container carries its bytes and
no mode, so nothing is refused on a mode this file system never held.

Measured against this machine's /bin/sh (bash 3.2.57), one container per
case: `cat sd`, `cat l`, `cat ./l`, `cat -n l`, `cat < d`, `exec 0<d; cat`,
`ln -s nope l; cat l`, `./s` at 755/700 and at 644/000, with and without a
shebang, and `./noexec.txt` at 644 all agree in stdout, stderr and status.
The row's own witness still holds: a 0755 `execok.sh` copied into /app
prints `ran` and exits 0, because the copy carries no mode to enforce.","paths":["packages/core/src/shell/shell.ts","packages/core/src/shell/commands/fileutils.ts","packages/core/src/shell/commands/builtins.ts"],"session_id":"adv7b-judge-shell-fs-1"}
